segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I've been doing some research into what people in Britain think of doctors,the ones who work in general practice- the first call for medical care - and comparingthis with .the situation in a couple of other countries.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I want to talk about the rationale behind what I decided to do.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now I had to set up my programmeof research in three different countriesso I approached postgraduatesin•my field in overseas departments,contactingthem by email, to organise 031 things for me at their end.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I thought I would have trouble recruitinghelp but in fact everyone was very willing and sometimestheir tutors got involved too.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I had to give my helpers clear instructionsabout what kind of sample population I wanted them to use.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I decided that people under 18 should be excluded because most of them are students or looking for their first job, and also I decided at this stage just to focus on men 032 who were in employment,and set up somethingfor people who didn't have jobs and for employedwomen later on as a separate investigation.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I specificallywanted to do a questionnaire,and interviewswith a focus group.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: With the questionnaire,rather than lim:ting it to one specific point, I wanted to include as much 033 variety as possible.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I know questionnairesare a very controlledway to do things but I thought I could do taped interviews later on to counteractthe effects of this.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And the focus group may also prove useful in future, by targeting subjects I can easily return to, as the participantstend to be more involved.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So I'm just collating the results now.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: At the moment it looks as if, in the UK, despite the fact 034 that newspaperscontinuallyreport that people are unhappywith medical care, in fact it is mainly the third level of care, which takes place in hospitals,that they are worried about.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Governmentreforms have been proposed at all levels and although their success is not guaranteed,long-term hospital care is in fact probably less of an issue than the media would have us believe.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: However, I've still got quite a bit of data to look at.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Certainly I will need to do more faMeaching researchthan I had anticipatedin order to 035 establish if peoplewant extra medical staff invested in the community,or if they want care to revert to fewer, but larger, key medical units.The solution may well be somethingthat can be easily implementedby those responsiblein local government,with central governmentsupport of course.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This first stage has proved very valuable though.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I was surprised by how willing most of the subjects were to get involved in the project - I had expected some unwillingnessto answer questions honestly.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But i was taken aback and rather concernedthat something I thought I'd set up very well didn't necessarilyseem that way to everyone in my own department. thought you might also be interested in some of the problems I encounteredin collecting my data.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There were odd cases that threw me - one of the subjects who I had approached while he was out shopping in town, decided to pull out when it came to the second round.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It was a shame as it was someonewho I would like to have interviewedmore closely.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: And one of the first-year students I interviewedwanted reassurancethat no names would be traceablefrom the answers.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I was so surprised, becausethey think nothing of telling you about themselvesand their opinions in seminar groups!

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Then, one of the people that I work with got a bit funny.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The questionswere quite personal and one minute he said he'd do it, then the next day he wouldn't, and in the end he did do !_!.It's hard not to get angry in that situation but I tried to keep focused on the overall picture in order to stay calm.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: The most bizarre case was a telephone interview I did with a teacher at a universityin France.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: He answeredall my questions in great detail - but then when I asked how much access he had to dangeroussubstanceshe wouldn't tell me exactly what his work involved. 040 It's a real eye-opener... lilill
